title: [finding] deployment/cli.mdx's ADR-0130 section states package-docs collection as one level under src/ — true but no longer the whole rule once #18965 lands, and the drift check cannot see it because the page restates the rule in prose
body:
Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat #6024 (`session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf`). ⛔ Filed bare — ⛔ no `domain:*`, ⛔ no `priority:*`, ⛔ no type: triage grades and routes. ⛔ Not a claim. ⛔ Not a ruling.

⭐ **Found by the at-tier contract reviewer of PR #19492** (record `5756127900`, facet ③), ⛔ not by this seat's own docs sweep — which looked at this exact page and **rejected it**. Why that matters is at the bottom.

⏱️ Every line below was read first-hand on `origin/main` `ef256e6a8f`. ⛔ Nothing is quoted from a report.

## The gap

`content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:614-626` describes how `os build` collects package docs under an ADR-0130 multi-package layout:

> Under an **ADR-0130 multi-package layout**, docs that moved into a package are collected too: a `src/<pkg>/docs/` directory whose `<pkg>` names one of the artifact's declared `packages[]` entries is read into **that package's own body** … A directory that matches **none** of the declared packages, or **more than one**, is still not read — that case keeps the warning that names the files it skipped and the spellings it tried, so it is never a silent `0 collected`.

That is an accurate description of the behaviour **`df0c856e01` (PR #18962) landed**: one level under `src/`, matched by `id` or its last dot-separated segment.

**PR #19492 (card #18965) changes the rule it describes** — on the maintainer's ruling at `5754492000`, `os build` now resolves each package's docs directory **from the registered packages at any depth**, not from a fixed one level. After that lands the page is **still true and no longer complete**:

| the page says | after #19492 |
| --- | --- |
| `src/<pkg>/docs/` — one level | resolution walks to **any depth** in search of a registered package |
| matched by `id` or its last segment | ⭐ **unchanged** — this half survives verbatim |
| a directory matching none *"is still not read"*, with the warning | in a multi-package tree it now **recurses deeper first**; the warning is what happens when the search finds nothing |
| a directory matching more than one is not read | now **refused with both candidates named** — the page's shape still holds |

⇒ ⛔ **no sentence on the page becomes false.** Every behaviour it asserts still happens. It simply stops being the whole rule, and a reader following it would believe a two-level layout is not collected when it now is.

## What this card asks

The section is re-stated against the landed rule — the any-depth resolution, the stopping condition, and what the warning now means. ⚠️ ⛔ **Not** a rider on PR #19492: that PR carries an at-tier contract review of record bound to head `4afa1e4669`, and a docs commit would move the head and void it. A docs-only follow-up is the cheap correct shape.

⚠️ **Check before writing**: at filing time #19492 is enqueued but not merged. Verify the delivery is on `origin/main` first — ⛔ the rule this card is about is the one that lands, not the one that is queued.

## ⭐ Why this seat's own sweep missed it, recorded because the miss is the instructive part

The docs-drift check listed this page, and this seat **rejected it on weak-anchor grounds**: the only reason given was *"via `node_modules` (literal, a string literal in `packageDirectoryCandidates`)"*, and a string literal named `node_modules` is not an assertion the page makes about the change. **That anchor reading was correct.**

The conclusion drawn from it was not. The page is affected because it **restates the rule in prose** — which shares no identifier with the emitter and is therefore invisible to the drift check on this run and on every run. The check says so about itself, in the very comment that listed the page:

> a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run.

⇒ ⭐ **"the anchor is weak" and "the page is unaffected" are different findings**, and this seat collapsed them. A page listed on a weak anchor still has to be read for a rule it might restate — the anchor decides only whether the *check* found it for a good reason.

## Related, ⛔ not duplicates

`doc-pages.mdx`, `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` and ADR-0046 describe only the flat `src/docs/` convention; the reviewer records that those have been incomplete since `df0c856e01`, i.e. **before** this change, so they are a separate and older gap.

## Dedupe

`deployment/cli.mdx ADR-0130 section one level` · `package docs page restates the fixed depth` · `cli.mdx docs collection any depth incomplete` · `drift check weak anchor page still restates the rule`

Searched `objectstack-ai/objectstack` for this family: 45 rows, all code-side (#18965, #19247, #18170, #18431) — **none about the docs page's prose**. The instrument returned live rows, so the near-zero is a reading. ⇒ ⛔ no duplicate.
